title: Collateral effects of the pandemic in oncology patients
summary:
The Covid-19 pandemic has put a heavy strain on healthcare, especially for people with cancer. Studies show that the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up care of cancer patients have been affected, leading to increased psychological distress. The “Collateral Effects in Pandemics” (CollPan) project is investigating these effects in more detail.

Lung cancer, pancreatic cancer and colorectal cancer are particularly affected. The pandemic may have affected the diagnosis and treatment of these cancers, which could lead to more deaths. The mental health of patients will also be examined.

Data from the Research Data Portal for Health (FDPG) will be used to analyze the impact of the pandemic on mortality and diagnosis of these cancers. The study compares the time before, during and after the pandemic. The aim is to find out how the pandemic has affected cancer care and what organizational changes have taken place.

The study uses data with and without broad consent and also evaluates the processes of data provision and analysis.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung

interventions.name: Patients with tumors of the respiratory tract (ICD-10 C34.-); Retrospective analysis of routine data from hospitals are used to examine the frequency of diagnostic and/or therapeutic measures in order to investigate the collateral effects of the pandemic.

Patients with tumors of the pancreas (ICD-10 C25.-); Retrospective analysis of routine data from hospitals are used to examine the frequency of diagnostic and/or therapeutic measures in order to investigate the collateral effects of the pandemic.

Patients with tumors of the colon (ICD-10 C18.-); Retrospective analysis of routine data from hospitals are used to examine the frequency of diagnostic and/or therapeutic measures in order to investigate the collateral effects of the pandemic.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
There was contact with a participating healthcare facility in the period from 01.04.2018 to 31.03.2023 and one of the following diagnosis categories: C18, C25 or C34
Exclusion criteria:
All data records, that do not match the inclusion criteria
